question.leadin: The continent of Europe is home to many notable seas of the world.
question.text: This sea in eastern Europe names the region containing Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia. Stockholm, Sweden, lies on the shores of this sea.
question.clue: The yearly Skane Market was a major trading event for herring in this body of water.

swap.text: This northern neighbor of Germany lies on the Jutland peninsula. It also controls Greenland.
swap.clue: This country's King Valedmar II wrote the Code of Jutland, this country's first constitution.

question.text: Viking expansion beyond Scandinavia included the founding of a permanent colony on Greenland by this father of Leif Erikson.
question.clue: During that exile, he established an estate at Brattahlith.

swap.text: The goal of Scott's expedition was to be the first men to reach the South Pole. When they arrived, however, they were devastated to learn that a crew led by this Norwegian had beaten them to it by four weeks.
swap.clue: This Norwegian explorer sailed the Fram to Antarctica in a 1911 expedition that was the first to reach the South Pole, beating Robert Falcon Scott's by one month. This explorer and Scott now co-name an American research station at the South Pole.

question.leadin: Before one battle in this war, the losing side's king was incapacitated by a leg injury received while personally scouting enemy redoubts.
question.text: Name this war during which Charles XII was defeated at the Battle of Poltava. This war ended with Peter the Great forcing Sweden to sign the Treaty of Nystad.
question.answerHtml: Great Northern War [or Second Northern War; prompt on Northern War]
question.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

swap.text: This Swedish High Chancellor succeeded Gustavus Adolphus as king after his death. He ruled during Queen Christina's regency and issued administrative reforms that prevented Sweden from becoming an absolute monarchy.
swap.clue: This man corresponded extensively with the Dutch merchant Samuel Blommaert ("BLOM-art") to set up a New World colony with his country's "South Company."

question.text: This ruler defended the Protestant cause during the Thirty Years' War as he led Sweden to become a major military force as well as one of the great powers of Europe. He famously defeated the Count of Tilly at the Battle of Breitenfeld.
question.clue: This man allegedly claimed that "the Lord God is my armor" before fighting without protection and dying at the Battle of Lutzen.

swap.leadin: This country once formed a dual monarchy with Norway.
swap.text: Name this Scandinavian nation that was led by Christian X in the early twentieth century.
swap.clue: It's not Norway, but English kings Harold Harefoot and Harthacanute were from this country.

question.text: The majority of prisoners rescued in the "White Buses" campaign were originally from this country, where Josef Terboven was installed as military governor during its Nazi occupation.
question.clue: Those operations targeted a plant at Vemork in this country's Telemark region which produced heavy water for nuclear weapons.

swap.text: Mannerheim's fortifications along the Karelian Isthmus, unsurprisingly dubbed the Mannerheim Line, enabled Finland to resist Soviet assault during the namesake season of 1939-1940. Afterwards, Mannerhim expanded his work to include the Salpa Line.
swap.clue: The invading side was expelled from the League of Nations as a result, and a major goal of the war was to cut off Germany's supply of iron ore.

question.text: The Battle of Dybbol in the Second Schleswig War took place in this region which makes up most of modern-day Denmark. John Jellicoe led British forces at an inconclusive World War I naval battle named for this body of land.
question.clue: Admiral Jellicoe's greatest triumph came at this May 31, 1916, naval engagement that saw the defeat of the German fleet under Reinhard Scheer.

swap.text: Until 1597, most of Tycho's observations were undertaken at this observatory, devoted to his Muse, on the Isle of Hven. It notably lacked a telescope.

question.leadin: This ruler put herself forward as a candidate for the elective Polish throne due to "herself being Catholic, an old maid and intending to remain one"
question.text: Identify this monarch often nicknamed the "Minerva of the North". This monarch argued for peace during the Thirty Years' War at the behest of her regent Axel Oxenstierna.
question.answerHtml: Queen Christina [or Drottning Kristina, accept Christina Augusta or Christina Alexandra, DO NOT reveal her title of “Queen of Sweden”]
question.clue: Although historians are not sure whether the abdication was influenced by a clandestine love for Cardinal Decio Azzolino, we do know that this ruler received educateion from Jorge Stiernhelm.

swap.text: Franklin Scott's "A Saint and a Queen" discusses Margaret and this Swedish saint, who created the "Fifteen O's" prayer and a namesake order open to men and women.

question.leadin: Arabic geographers such as Al-Biruni named the Baltic Sea after this term, which likely first appeared in Greek, derived from an obscure Norse term meaning "sworn companion."
question.text: Give this term used to describe a variety of Scandinavian peoples in Nestor's Primary Chronicle. In 989 AD, the rebel Bardas Phokas suffered a stroke while facing a military unit named for this term that was first organized under Basil II.
question.answerHtml: Varangian [or várangoi; accept varyazi, væringjar, or varyahy; accept Varangian Guard; do not accept or prompt on “Vikings”]
question.clue: One theory of Russian religious history points to these people as the means by which the self-sacrificing priest-king entered the Russian pagan pantheon shortly before the spread of Christianity, a transplant from the Norse Odin.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about popular assemblies across medieval Europe.
swap.text: This country's assembly, which met by the Law Rock, signed the Old Covenant with Haakon IV that maintained its function but required royal assent.
swap.clue: Local lords called godr in this region met at the Law Rock, over which the Lawspeaker presided.

question.text: For Frederick I's rule and some years afterwards the riksdag was dominated by these two political parties, one of which assumed control of parliament in 1738 before giving way to the other in 1765.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about insane CIA Cold War plots that did not involve exploding cigars or acoustic kitties.
swap.text: This place was long thought to contain a lost hydrogen bomb after a secret mission crashed at Thule Air Base. Project Iceworm wanted to build launch sites under this territory of Denmark, which is the world's largest island.
swap.clue: Henrik Kauffman signed a 1941 treaty with the United States paving the way for the establishment of Thule Airbase on this island.

question.leadin: He had to deal with revolts in Dalarna and one led by Nils Dacke, and at the Diet of Vasteras, he confiscated the property of Sweden's Catholic Church.
question.text: Name this founder of the Vasa dynasty who signed the Treaty of Malmo with Christian II, thus relieving Sweden of Denmark's rule in the Kalmar Union.

swap.text: The Finnish-German alliance did not stay intact, and in this 1944-45 war, Germany decided to secure Petsamo while their 20th Mountain Army got consistently owned in the namesake geographical region.
swap.clue: After signing an armistice with the Soviet Union in 1944, Finland fought this war in order to expel German troops from its territory.
